data.title: Defense-Evasion Registry Modification
data.summary: The sample edits registry keys as a defense-evasion step distinct from persistence — disabling a security feature's configuration, hiding its own keys from the default registry editor view, or altering a policy key.
data.description:
This covers registry writes whose purpose is evasion rather than relaunch: flipping a
security feature's enabled flag, writing a key with an embedded null character that the
standard Registry Editor fails to display correctly, or modifying a Group Policy-backed
key that a security control reads at startup. It is distinguished from persistence-related
registry writes (see run keys) by what the key controls, not by the API used to write it.
data.recommendation:
* Diff registry state against a known-good baseline focused on security-feature configuration keys, not only autorun locations.
* Check for embedded null characters or other malformed key/value names that standard tooling may fail to render.
* Treat any write to a security-control configuration key from a non-administrative or unexpected process as high-confidence malicious.
data.short_recommendation: Diff registry state against a baseline focused on security-feature configuration keys, not only autorun locations.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Wrote a value disabling a security feature's real-time scanning flag under its policy-backed registry key.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Modified a security-feature configuration key to disable a protection flag read only at service startup.
